official.deadline_central_display: 9 September 2026, 3:00pm UK time (2027 round close date)
official.deadline_note: No separate institutional deadline is published, but the host organisation's delegated approver must approve the completed application in Flexi-Grant before the closing date; referees and the Head of Department are recommended to finish at least 5 working days earlier.
official.application_cycle: 2027 round of the University Research Fellowship (opened 14 July 2026, closed 9 September 2026); fellowships expected to commence between 1 October 2027 and 1 January 2028. No dates are published for the following round.
official.status_note: The scheme page shows Status: Closed for the 2027 round, open 14 July 2026 and close 09 September 2026, with decisions by 31 May 2027; the Republic of Ireland scheme notes give expected results in July 2027 and offer letters in August 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Republic of Ireland scheme notes publish no tuition contribution for the fellowship holder: the award funds the Research Fellow's salary and research costs. Tuition-type support appears only for a requested 4-year PhD studentship, where a stipend of EUR 25,000 per year and university fees of up to EUR 5,750 may be requested.
benefits: Eight-year independent research fellowship hosted within a Research Ireland Eligible Research Body in the Republic of Ireland
Research Fellow's basic salary costs and associated on-costs funded at 100% contribution, on the Research Ireland Grants Team Member budgeting scale, including PRSI and employer pension

Overhead costs equivalent to 30% of the value of the award excluding equipment, plus research expenses of up to EUR 720,000 over 8 years with an expected maximum of EUR 90,000 per annum and carry-over of underspend
Contribution to research assistance/PDRA salary and to 4-year PhD studentships (EUR 25,000 stipend per year plus university fees up to EUR 5,750)
Funding for relocation and visa costs for the applicant and dependants (partner and children), and up to EUR 8,000 over the fellowship for public engagement activities
Royal Society career development, training, networking and engagement opportunities, and access to the Global Talent Visa fast-track endorsement
eligibility: Early career, postdoctoral researchers of any nationality with between three and eight years of actual research experience since their PhD (date the degree was approved by the board of graduate studies) by the closing date of the round

Cases of exceptional talent with less than three years of research experience may be considered case by case, requiring a Head of Department support letter submitted and flagged to the Grants team separately from and prior to the application
Research within the Royal Society's remit of natural sciences, including but not limited to biological research, biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics

The fellowship must be hosted within a Research Ireland Eligible Research Body situated in the Republic of Ireland (universities, technological universities, institutes of technology and independent not-for-profit public research organisations)

Not for postdoctoral researchers who already lead a research group or are named as lead applicant (Principal Investigator) on an external award, nor for academic staff holding a tenure track faculty position or permanent academic post (including proleptic position) in a university or not-for-profit research organisation

Not for current or previous holders of a nationally competitive research fellowship equivalent to a URF, defined as awarded through a national open competition, of four or more years duration, portable to any host organisation, providing salary and research costs/staff support, and intended to enable independence
requirements: Applications can only be submitted online through the Royal Society's Flexi-Grant system at grants.royalsociety.org; paper applications are not accepted and late applications will not be accepted
A research proposal and costs for eight years must be submitted, fully justified, with equipment costing more than EUR 25,000 requiring additional justification

Two supporting contributions are required through Flexi-Grant: a Head of Department statement of support and one nominated referee's confidential reference, and references must be submitted in English
An ORCID identifier is a mandatory requirement at the application submission stage

The Head of Department and nominated referee cannot be the same person, and the referee must not be a named collaborator in the application, a member of the assessment Panel, or a member of the Royal Society's Council
The host organisation's delegated approver must approve the completed application before the closing date, with every participant section marked complete
documents: Application form completed in Flexi-Grant (eleven pages), including the applicant career summary, research proposal and eight-year costed budget
Head of Department statement of support covering suitability, space, protected time, status and benefits, plus additional statements if PhD studentship or research staff costs are requested
One nominated referee's confidential reference, in English, submitted through Flexi-Grant
Budget justifications for salary, research expenses and PhD studentships, with the inflation field completed as 'N/A'
Completed diversity monitoring section and host organisation approval by the delegated approver
selection_criteria: The scientific track record of the applicant commensurate with research experience: past achievements, research career to date, publication record, likely contribution to the field and future potential to become a research leader

The scientific merit, originality, significance and quality of the proposed research, the clarity and originality of the five-year project alongside a broader eight-year vision, and a clear plan and justification for the research budget
The suitability of the host institution, including appropriate expertise, equipment and resources, research environment and support for career development

Mid-fellowship review criteria for years six to eight: updated track record including first or senior authored papers, evidence of independent research and additional grants secured, quality and originality of the proposed project, and suitability of the host institution
coverage: Research Fellow's basic salary costs and associated on-costs (100% contribution), at the Research Ireland Research Fellow scale for years one to five and the Senior Research Fellow scale for years six to eight after successful mid-term review
Overhead costs, equivalent to 30% of the value of the award excluding equipment

Research expenses up to EUR 720,000 over 8 years, covering consumables, travel and subsistence, open access, relocation expenses, visa costs for the applicant and dependants, software and recurring computing costs, fieldwork, specialist publications, consultancy fees, summer students and access charges
Directly incurred equipment at 100% contribution, including delivery, installation, spares, software procurement and maintenance
Research assistance and PDRA costs at the Research Ireland Team Member Salary Scales, and 4-year PhD studentships including stipend and fees
Public engagement costs up to EUR 8,000 over the duration of the fellowship
application_method: Register and complete the application form on Flexi-Grant at grants.royalsociety.org
Invite the Head of Department and one nominated referee through the participants tab and monitor their completion status
Optionally invite a research support contact from the Irish host organisation to check the finances
Submit the application for approval by the host organisation's delegated approver before the closing date of 9 September 2026 at 3:00pm UK time
official.application_route: Apply through the Royal Society's Flexi-Grant system, with the Head of Department statement and one referee completed and the host organisation's approval in place before the closing date.
official.study_mode: Full-time or part-time; the fellowship is flexible and can be held below 1.0 FTE for health reasons or caring responsibilities, with costs entered at 1.0 FTE and adjusted later
official.citizenship_residency: Open to postdoctoral researchers of any nationality; the fellowship must be hosted at a Research Ireland Eligible Research Body situated in the Republic of Ireland, and candidates are not required to move institution but must explain their route to independence if staying
official.international_eligibility: Applicants can be of any nationality; those requiring a visa are eligible to apply for a Global Talent Visa under the fast-track process of endorsement, and visa and relocation costs for the applicant and dependants are eligible costs
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Research must be within the Royal Society's remit of natural sciences (biological research and biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics, physics and related areas). The Society does not support clinical or interventional research on humans at the individual or group level, social sciences, or humanities; submissions from clinically qualified scientists may be considered.
official.research_requirement: Applicants must submit a research proposal and costs for eight years; the research proposal document is limited to four pages including all images and references, and costs for years six to eight are subject to the mid-fellowship review at the start of year four
official.duration: 8 years, with years 6 to 8 subject to satisfactory progress demonstrated in a mid-fellowship review at the start of year four
official.description: The Royal Society - Research Ireland University Research Fellowship is a partnership award giving outstanding early career researchers from the Republic of Ireland the opportunity to establish an independent research career, hosted within a Research Ireland Eligible Research Body and funded by Research Ireland. Applicants from the Republic of Ireland are assessed alongside candidates from the UK through the normal Royal Society peer review process, and successful candidates are awarded a fellowship by the Royal Society, the cost of which is met by Research Ireland.
official.program_type: University Research Fellowship (URF): a long-term, independent early career research fellowship

not_confirmed: english_requirement: no IELTS, TOEFL or medium-of-instruction score is published; the only English rule on the official pages is that references must be submitted in English

Total award value in euro: the Republic of Ireland scheme notes cap research expenses at EUR 720,000 and fund 100% of salary plus 30% overheads, but publish no overall euro maximum (the GBP 1,907,400 maximum quoted on the scheme page applies to UK-based awards funded by BIST)
Dates for the next round after 2027: none are published
Salary point values in euro, which sit in the Research Ireland Grant Budget Policy and Team Member Salary Scales rather than the scheme notes
verification.notes: Amounts and dates were read from the Republic of Ireland URF 2027 scheme notes PDF and the University Research Fellowship scheme page on royalsociety.org, cross-checked against the Royal Society application dates page; the 2027 round closed on 9 September 2026 and the eligible-host rule was checked against Research Ireland's Eligible Research Bodies policy.

applicant_utility.summary: The money here is an employer-style package, not a studentship: 100% of your salary on the Research Ireland Research Fellow scale plus 30% overheads and up to EUR 720,000 of research expenses across eight years, so your real job is convincing an Irish department to host you and to say so in writing. Years six to eight are not guaranteed at the award stage - they are released only after the mid-fellowship review at the start of year four, so pitch an eight-year arc rather than a five-year project. Republic of Ireland applicants are ranked alongside UK candidates in the same panels, where success rates have run at roughly 6 to 7% of eligible applications over the last four years. Timetable it backwards from a 9 September close: referees and the Head of Department should be finished at least five working days earlier, and your host's approver still has to sign off before the deadline.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Natural scientists three to eight years post-PhD who want a long independent platform at an Irish university or research body and can win a head of department's written backing and protected research time.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your intended host appears on Research Ireland's list of Eligible Research Bodies, and that the department will commit in writing to space, equipment, protected time and equal status with academic staff
Recalculate your research experience from the PhD approval date, deducting career breaks with the published top-up rules, before you touch the form

Line up one referee who is not a named collaborator, a panel member or a Council member, and confirm both their and your Head of Department's Flexi-Grant sections will be complete five working days before the deadline

Build the eight-year budget against the Research Ireland Team Member Salary Scales, expecting around EUR 90,000 of research expenses per year within the EUR 720,000 ceiling, with every equipment item over EUR 25,000 separately justified
Cut the research proposal to the four-page limit including figures and references, list your most relevant publications (up to 20), and register an ORCID iD before submitting
Invite the host's research office in the optional Research Support role so the finance pages are checked before you submit
common_rejection_risks: Failing the September to October eligibility screening: holding a permanent or tenure-track post, already leading a group or external award as PI, or holding an equivalent national fellowship such as the Research Ireland Pathway or Investigators programmes
Never actually submitting because a participant was left 'incomplete' in Flexi-Grant or the host organisation's approval was not in place by the deadline
An exceptional-talent claim for under three years of experience where the Head of Department letter was not emailed to urf@royalsociety.org and flagged before the application
A proposal that sells only the first five years with no credible eight-year strategy, or budget lines left unjustified, which the panel treats as a funding risk
Poor subject tag selection, which routes the application to the wrong Research Appointment Panel and to reviewers without matching expertise
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Your salary, overheads, research expenses and your own relocation and visa costs are funded, but relocation and visa costs for your research group are explicitly ineligible, teaching and administrative load beyond the supported six hours per teaching week is not funded by this award, and the institution may top up your salary only at its own discretion. If you are moving from abroad, plan personal relocation logistics beyond the covered costs yourself.
document_audit: The Head of Department statement and the referee's reference cannot come from the same person, and both must be written in English

The Head of Department statement must spell out office and laboratory space, access to equipment, software and facilities, protected fellowship time, and equal status and benefits, with extra statements if you request PhD or research staff costs
Every budget heading needs its own justification - salary, research expenses and PhD studentships - and the inflation field must literally read 'N/A'
Equipment requests need Head of Department confirmation of your priority access, extra justification above EUR 25,000, and a VAT check before you request the item
All diversity monitoring questions must be answered or marked 'prefer not to say', or the form will not let you submit
alerts: The 2027 round closed on 9 September 2026 at 3:00pm UK time and no dates are published for the following round, so prepare against a recurring July to September window
Years six to eight are conditional on the mid-fellowship review at the start of year four, so the eight-year budget is a plan you will have to defend twice
Fellowships start between 1 October 2027 and 1 January 2028; a permanent post or equivalent fellowship accepted after the deadline is allowed, but you must resign from it to take up the URF
Interviews for shortlisted applicants are in person at the Royal Society in London during 13 to 29 April 2027, with results notified in July 2027 and offer letters in August 2027
Republic of Ireland applicants compete in the same review as UK candidates, with recent success rates of 7% (2022/23), 6.4% (2023/24), 6.8% (2024/25) and 6.3% (2025/26)
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Build the form in Flexi-Grant, invite your Head of Department and one referee as participants, wait until both show as complete, then submit for host organisation approval - only after the approver signs off before the deadline does the application enter eligibility checks, panel review, independent peer review and the April interview.
